items.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: Rudolf Serkin wanted me to come and live with him and study and have tutors and a governess and stuff like that.

ctx.x: It sounds to me like you have a really healthy ego, like you know what you like and you feel good about your playing, but you’re also able to fit in with all these other musicians and artists.

Yeah. Well it’s not that I didn’t work on that because I had a terrible problem with ego and conceitedness being an only child growing up in this atmosphere in New York where I was a prodigy playing concerts. You know, Rudolf Serkin wanted me to come and live with him and study and have tutors and a governess and stuff like that. And my father saying, “Do you want to do that?” I said, “No, I want to keep my friends, I want to play sports, I want to go to school.” I mean a lot of different probabilities could have…
Do you still feel that way?
